answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to post a refundable stake and earn reputation only through completed jobs that counterparties validate, with disputes decided by randomly selected, stake-bearing peers. A sybil cannot gain influence merely by creating accounts: it must lock capital in every ivory-tower identity, then risk losing stake for collusive reviews or fraud. To forge a credible network, the attacker must fund many deposits and sustain believable work; detection can slash linked stakes, while the resulting ripple of lost trust makes those identities costly to reuse.
